title: Strict-transform chart formula localizes
statement:
Let $f:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, $a\in I$, $b=f(a)$, $J=IB$, and $s\in B$. Set
$$R=C_a^{\mathrm{st}}(A,B,I),\quad T=B[J/b],\quad R'=C_a^{\mathrm{st}}(A,B_s,I),\quad T'=B_s[JB_s/(b/1)].$$
Write $g:R\to T$ and $g':R'\to T'$ for the comparisons of [def-nagata-strict-transform-chart-comparison]. Let $\alpha:R_s\xrightarrow{\sim}R'$ be the canonical source identification of [lemma-nagata-strict-transform-chart-localization-data], and let $\beta:T_s\to T'$ be the canonical map induced by $B\to B_s$, sending $y\in B$ to $y/1$ and $z/b$ ($z\in J$) to $(z/1)/(b/1)$. Here localization at $s$ always means localization at its structural image.

The constructed localized comparison $g_s=(\overline\sigma_a)_s:R_s\to T_s$ of [def-nagata-strict-transform-chart-comparison-localized] equals the comparison constructed directly from the localized data, under these identifications:
$$\beta\circ g_s=g'\circ\alpha.$$
The map $\beta$ is an isomorphism, so equivalently $\beta\circ g_s\circ\alpha^{-1}=g'$. For localization at an element of $A$, use its image in $B$. The equality is preserved under the canonical tensor-product and iterated-localization presentation transports specified in [def-nagata-strict-transform-chart-comparison-localized], including further localization of the chart rings.

proof.text: Put $C=B\otimes_A A[I/a]$ and $C'=B_s\otimes_A A[I/a]$, with quotient maps $q:C\to R$ and $q':C'\to R'$. The canonical isomorphism in [lemma-nagata-strict-transform-chart-localization-data] gives $\alpha:R_s\simeq R'$. Its canonical map is induced by the coefficient-localization map $y\otimes u\mapsto(y/1)\otimes u$, hence $\alpha(q(y\otimes u)/1)=q'((y/1)\otimes u)$. This records the map as well as its isomorphism property; no injectivity of $B\to B_s$ is assumed.

proof.text: Construct the target map without assuming localization is injective. The localization universal property gives $B_b\to(B_s)_{b/1}$, sending $y/b^n$ to $(y/1)/(b/1)^n$. Its restriction to $T$ lands in $T'$: by [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring], $T$ is generated as a $B$-algebra by $z/b$ for $z\in J$, and the displayed images are generators of $T'$ or coefficients in $B_s$. Thus it gives $k:T\to T'$. The image $k(s)=s/1$ is a unit of $T'$, with inverse the coefficient $1/s\in B_s$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-universal-property] to $k$ gives $\beta:T_s\to T'$ with $\beta(t/s^n)=k(t)(s/1)^{-n}$. This argument uses only the specified subalgebra generators and the cited universal property.

proof.text:
Compare maps before the quotient. By [def-nagata-strict-chart-to-extended-blowup-chart], both $gq$ and $g'q'$ are the maps obtained from the coefficient map and the chart map by the tensor-product universal property. The two maps from $C$ to $T'$ obtained by going through $R$ and $R'$ agree on $y\otimes1$: both give $y/1$. They agree on $1\otimes(x/a)$ for $x\in I$: both give $(f(x)/1)/(b/1)$. The algebra $A[I/a]$ is generated by these fractions over $A$, so the chart-factor maps agree. Tensor-product uniqueness now gives equality on $C$. Since $q$ is surjective, this gives, for every $r\in R$,
$$k(g(r))=g'(\alpha(r/1)).$$
Here the comparison on the quotient is exactly the induced map specified by [def-nagata-strict-transform-chart-comparison]; the argument does not use an uncited assertion of naturality.

proof.text: By the definition of the localized comparison, $g_s(r/1)=g(r)/1$. Step 3 therefore says that $\beta g_s$ and $g'\alpha$ agree on every $r/1\in R_s$. Apply the uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-universal-property] with source ring $R$, localization element the image of $s$, and target $T'$. The two ring maps are equal. Explicitly their common value at $r/s^n$ is $g'(\alpha(r/1))(s/1)^{-n}$. This proves the asserted equality on all fractions, not merely on the unlocalized generators.

proof.text:
Apply [prop-nagata-strict-transform-chart-iso] to both $A\to B$ and $A\to B_s$: $g$ and $g'$ are isomorphisms. The inverse $g^{-1}:T\to R$ takes the structural image of $s$ to that of $s$, because $g$ is a $B$-algebra map by its defining tensor construction. Localize $g^{-1}$ by the universal property to obtain $h:T_s\to R_s$. The composites $hg_s$ and $g_sh$ fix the images of $R$ and $T$, respectively, so localization uniqueness makes them identities. Thus $g_s$ is invertible. From step 4,
$$\beta=g'\alpha h,$$
which is a composite of three isomorphisms. This proves that the canonical target map is the required identification, rather than assuming this identification at the start.

source.place: Proof of order 161: equality on pure tensors and chart generators, then the equivalence property; expanded with Stacks Tags 052Q (definition-blow-up), 0BIP (lemma-blowup-base-change), and 00CP (proposition-universal-property-localization)

proof.text: For $s\in A$, apply the result to $f(s)\in B$; the denominators are the structural images specified by [def-nagata-strict-transform-chart-comparison-localized]. Set $F=\beta g_s\alpha^{-1}:R'\to T'$. Step 4 gives $F=g'$. For canonical presentation isomorphisms $v:R'\simeq\widetilde R$ and $u:T'\simeq\widetilde T$, composing this equality gives $uFv^{-1}=ug'v^{-1}$, exactly the transported comparison. For further localization at any chart element $c\in R'$, use the target $T'_{g'(c)}$. Since $F(c)=g'(c)$ is a unit in that target, both maps extend by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-universal-property] to maps $R'_c\to T'_{g'(c)}$. Each sends $r/c^n$ to $g'(r)/g'(c)^n$, so uniqueness makes the extensions equal. Thus the same equality holds after further chart localization with the matched target denominator; $c$ need not come from $A$ or $B$.

blueprint_notes.label: status
blueprint_notes.text:
**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the strict transform is
supplied by the API of
`WeilConjectures/Compactification/StrictTransform.lean` —
`AlgebraicGeometry.strictTransform`, its closed immersion
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.isClosedImmersion_pullbackLift_blowup_comap`,
and the pullback square
`AlgebraicGeometry.isPullback_strictTransformOpen` — so the
strict-transform chart rings and their cocycle are never assembled by hand.

blueprint_update.statement:
The constructed localized comparison $(\overline\sigma_a)_s$ equals the
strict-transform chart comparison constructed directly from the localized
data.

proof.text:
Localization commutes with the tensor product and with the power-torsion
quotient by [lemma-nagata-power-torsion-localization]. Both maps send
every pure tensor and every generator $x/a$ to the same fraction. Ring-map
extensionality gives the equality, and
[prop-nagata-strict-transform-chart-iso] supplies the equivalence
property on both sides.
